facts.text: The class opens a pyserial port with the port, baud rate and timeout given to __init__ and keeps the port object in serial_port
send() appends a newline to the command and reads one reply line
output_on() and output_off() send OUTPut ON and OUTPut OFF, and get_outputState() sends OUTPut?
set_voltage() writes VOLTage with three decimals and get_voltage() reads VOLTage?
set_voltage_limit() writes VOLTage:LIMit with three decimals and the code comments a 1 V minimum
set_current() writes CURRent with three decimals and get_current() reads CURRent?
set_current_limit() writes CURRent:LIMit with three decimals and the code comments a 100 mA minimum
get_all_parametrs() sends MEASure:ALL:INFO? and returns the reply unparsed
The upstream example names the tested model SPE3051 as a 30 V, 5 A, 150 W supply
The README describes the package as a SCPI driver for the OWON power supply, tested on the SPA3051 model, connected as a virtual COM port

measures.description: Raw reply of MEASure:ALL:INFO? (the full measurement block, unparsed)
measures.name: all_parameters

operator_required.name: voltage_setpoint
operator_required.reason: the clone states no complete voltage range for the generic OwonPowerSupply class: example.py:4 names 30 V only for the tested SPE3051 and the class declares no model; the site supplies the range of the installed unit

operator_required.name: current_setpoint
operator_required.reason: the clone states no complete current range for the generic OwonPowerSupply class: example.py:4 names 5 A only for the tested SPE3051 and the class declares no model; the site supplies the range of the installed unit

operator_required.name: voltage_limit
operator_required.reason: owon_ps.py:77 comments a 1 V minimum but states no upper bound for the generic class; the site supplies the range of the installed unit

operator_required.name: current_limit
